Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

direct adjective

of a person or what they say: frank, straightforward

also frank, frankly, straightforward, outspoken, get to the point, don’t beat about the bush, without mincing words, not mince words, plainly, candid

classical

Cic. Rep. 3.26: quem apertum et simplicem volumus esse
Traupman 153: frank, apertus
Traupman 150
Traupman 286
Traupman 318

apertus, aperta, apertum

adjective (participle of aperiō), declension

open, frank, straightforward

Plainly, frankly: apertē.

Other words

  • simplex, simplicis — straightforward, candid, without guile

    adjective, third declension, one ending · classical · Cic. Rep. 3.26; Sen. Ep. 49.12: vēritātis simplex ōrātiō est

    Frankly is simpliciter: simpliciter et līberē (Plin. Ep. 1.13.2, Lewis & Short).

  • ambāgēs mittere — to stop beating about the bush, to come to the point

    phrase: ambāgēs, ambāgum f. pl., roundabout talk · also used · classical · Plaut. Cist. 747: ambāgēs, mulier, mitte atque hoc age; Hor. S. 2.5.9: missīs ambāgibus, without beating about the bush

    Ambāgēs are roundabout ways, of a road or of talk. Terence’s answer to a rigmarole: mitte: ad rem redī, drop it, get to the point (Heaut. 319).

  • sine fūcō ac fallāciīs — without mincing words, without pretence or deceit

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.1: sine fūcō ac fallāciīs (Lewis & Short s.v. fallācia); Traupman 103: without mincing words, sine fūcō ac fallāciīs

    Fūcus is rouge, paint on the face: “without paint and tricks”.

  • candidus, candida, candidum — candid, open, sincere

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 150; Hor. Ep. 1.4.1: candide jūdex (Lewis & Short); Traupman 286

    Properly “shining white”.

  • līberior, līberius — outspoken, rather free

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 156

    The comparative of līber, “rather free (in speech)”.

  • candidē — frankly, sincerely

    also used · classical · Traupman 318

Examples

  • sed quaesō, ambāgēs, mulier, mitte atque hoc age. ēloquere, unde haec sunt tibi, cito, crepundia

    but please, woman, stop beating about the bush and attend to this. Tell me, quickly: where did you get these trinkets?Plaut. Cist. 747–748

  • Quās, malum, ambāgēs mihi narrāre occipit? — Syre, vērum hic dīcit; mitte: ad rem redī.

    What’s this rigmarole he’s started telling me? — Syrus, he’s right: drop it and get to the point.Ter. Heaut. 318–319

  • vēritātis simplex ōrātiō est

    the language of truth is simpleSen. Ep. 49.12

See also direct, simple.
